questions.q: What five numbers does a box-and-whisker plot summarize a distribution into?
options: The minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum
The mean, mode, range, variance, and standard deviation
The sum, count, average, minimum, and maximum
Five arbitrary percentile values chosen by the analyst
questions.explain: A box plot's box spans the first to third quartile with the median marked inside, while the whiskers extend toward the minimum and maximum (or a 1.5x IQR cutoff).

questions.q: What does the box itself represent in a box-and-whisker plot?
options: The middle 50 percent of the data, from the first quartile to the third quartile
The full range of every value in the dataset
Only the single median value
The average plus or minus one standard deviation
questions.explain: The box spans the interquartile range — from Q1 to Q3 — representing the middle 50% of the data, with a line inside marking the median.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between the two whisker configurations Tableau offers?
options: One extends whiskers only to points within 1.5x the interquartile range (flagging anything beyond as an outlier dot), while the other stretches whiskers to the true minimum and maximum with no separate outlier marks
One configuration only works with dates, the other only with measures
One shows quartiles, the other shows only the mean
There is no practical difference between the two options
questions.explain: The 1.5x IQR convention isolates genuine statistical outliers as separate points, while the max-extent option simply stretches the whiskers to the data's true min/max.

questions.q: Why might a box plot reveal something a bar chart of average discount per segment would hide?
options: Because segments can share nearly identical averages while having very different spreads — a box plot shows spread directly, while a bar chart of averages shows only the single average number
Because bar charts cannot use the Discount field at all
Because box plots always use a different dataset than bar charts
Bar charts and box plots always show identical information
questions.explain: A bar chart of averages collapses each group to one number and loses all sense of spread — a box plot puts each group's spread front and center alongside its median.

questions.q: How does a box plot's use case differ from a histogram's, even though both show distribution?
options: A histogram shows one distribution's full shape in detail, while a box plot compresses that shape to five numbers so several groups can be compared side by side at once
A box plot can only be built from a single measure with no dimensions
A histogram cannot be built using Show Me
They are functionally identical chart types with different names
questions.explain: A histogram is best at showing one group's full distribution shape, while a box plot trades that detail for the ability to line up medians and spreads across multiple groups at a glance.
